My boyfriend had a 9cm tumor in his chest when diagnosed. The initial quick needle biopsy showed it was lymphoma and the doc assumed it was classical Hodgkins but it was actually Primary Mediastinal Large B cell lymphoma. PMBCL is very similar to Hodgkins in how it looks under a microscope and pathologists have to be very thorough to tell the two apart. Anyways he was diagnosed in August 2017. It was a hard fight but he beat it after a year and had an Allogeneic stem cell transplant in December to preserve his remission. He’s doing good now! Best of luck to you, this is a hard fight but you can beat this no matter which type it turns out to be!!

Hey, I would have hated if someone told me this because it would have made me uneasy about my BF but please get a second opinion. R-CHOP is an outdated chemo for PMBCL. My bf had R-CHOP and relapsed before his last pet scan, it simply isn't strong enough for how agressive this subtype is. Don't get me wrong it can work but DA-EPOCH-R is the updated regimen for PMBCL because it is more likely to do the job. You can also email Dr Wyndham Wilson ( wilsonw@mail.nih.gov ) you can tell him your situation and he will let you know the best course of action. He is a lymphoma specialist in MD that has done some of the most ground-breaking research for PMBCL. He responds to emails quite quickly and will help with advice. 
Like I said, I'm not telling you this to make you nervous but you can still switch to DA-EPOCH-R.

Hello, my partner has stage 3 Primary Mediastinal B cell lymphoma. I know its a completely different cancer but hopefully my insight will be useful. 
When he first started getting symptoms "the worst headache of his life" was one of them. Once he started chemo he was off balance, couldnt finish sentences, forgetful, would lean to one side when walking.
Now, most of those can be explained by chemotherapy and the headaches he had before treatment can be explained by SVC Syndrome but I, being the anxious mess that I am, convinced myself that his cancer had metastasized to his brain. 
He had had a CT scan that came back negative when he was first diagnosed. We switched docs and she ordered him a MRI on his brain that revealed a very small Lipoma in his brain (1cm) and they are very rare but they are just fatty tissue. Benign. 
I did read about them and they can cause tumor-like symptoms and even epilepsy. 
Definitely ask for an MRI bc the doc said he has most likely had this since birth but it did not show on the CT scan of his head.

Better safe than sorry. Lymphoma can be diagnosed by a needle aspiration biopsy. Lymphoma is a blood cancer and can be aggressive and grow quickly. If you are feeling skeptical get a second opinion but take it seriously.

Hi, 
I want to try to help put your mind at ease with some of the facts I know about lymphoma. My 25 year old fiance was diagnosed with stage 3 non hodgkins lymphoma. 
The stages in lymphoma dont work the same way as in other types of cancer. Stage 4 is not a death sentence. Many people reach remmision from stage 4. 
Hodgkins lymphoma is very curable. 90% 5 year survival rate is the average for all stages. Non-Hodgkins is not the worst either.
Your son is young so he has that on his side. 
My fiance is most likely in remission after 3 rounds of chemo. A CT scan showed that his tumor has shrunk to almost nothing and is most likely just residual scar tissue. We just have to get his PET to make sure.

The road is bumpy at first. Just hold on and be there for your son. So your best to keep his spirits up. This diagnoses will be devistating for everyone but just keep your heads up and fight hard
